mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative when UNRATE falls below 4% in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market, it suggests economic strength that may boost equity returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Forward returns are not positively correlated with joint labor strength (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 2% annually signals strong economic activity, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when INDPRO growth exceeds 2% in >30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High real estate investment (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when HOUST is high in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) may signal economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in >30% of cases when INDPRO declines sharply.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high and GDP growth (GDPC1) is low, it may indicate economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in >40% of cases with high FEDFUNDS and low GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real federal spending (RSAFS) may indicate reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in >30% of cases when RSAFS declines sharply.
